item.title: Shooting 101: Do Pistol Grip Safeties Make It Safer or a Liability?
item.description: Grip safeties on a pistol have been around since at least the introduction of the 1911 pistol, with at least one revolver using them in the late 1800’s. They still exist on most 1911 pistols today, as well as a few others. But do they make your pistol safer? Or are they a liability? Grip Safeties on a Pistol The prevailing thought was that the grip safety was added so the 1911 could be safely fired (not into the horse) one-handed. This was a general requirement for the cavalry. item.description: There were a variety of new ARs and AR pistols this year at SHOT Show. item.title: Classic Steel: The Smith & Wesson 5906 is a Testament to the Wonder Nine
item.description: How do you define a wonder nine? To me, a Wonder Nine is a semi-automatic, hammer-fired, all-metal pistol with a double-stack magazine. As the world transitioned to striker-fired, polymer-frame guns, we said goodbye to new Wonder Nine designs. One of the last was the S&W 5906, a Smith & Wesson third-generation pistol. item.title: Magpul’s New Sub-Compact RG9 For The Ruger RXM
item.description: The Ruger RXM has quietly become one of the more interesting polymer-frame pistols on the market, thanks to its modular Fire Control Insert and accessible price point. Now, Magpul is pushing the concept even further with the launch of its Enhanced Handgun Grip (EHG) RG9 Sub-Compact Grip module. A compact, carry-friendly frame that shrinks the RXM platform while keeping the shootability and customization that made the pistol appealing in the first place. item.title: Ares Gear Refreshes Its Website & Expands Vision
item.description: Ares Gear has long been a quiet benchmark in the duty and EDC world. If you’ve spent time around serious shooters, cops, or hard-use civilians, you’ve probably heard the Aegis belt mentioned with a tone usually reserved for mission-critical kit. Now, the U.S.-based company is stepping into a new chapter with the launch of a refreshed website—and a clear roadmap for growth.
